classification.difficultyReason: Visualise six congruent square pyramids sharing an interior apex and communicate the decomposition in a drawing.

content.prompt: Show with a drawing how a cube can be cut up into six identical square pyramids.

answer.short: Use each of the six cube faces as a pyramid’s square base, with all six pyramids sharing the centre of the cube as their apex.
answer.worked: Mark the centre $O$ of the cube and join it to all eight vertices. Each cube face and $O$ form a square pyramid. The six square bases are identical, and each apex lies directly above its base’s centre at the same perpendicular distance. Thus the six pyramids are identical and together fill the cube without overlapping interiors. The cuts lie in the triangular faces formed by $O$ and each cube edge.

spec.description: Cube with its centre joined to all eight vertices. Solid strokes show visible cube edges, dashed strokes show hidden cube edges, and dotted construction segments show the six-pyramid decomposition.
spec.mathematics: Each of the six square faces is the base of one pyramid whose apex is the cube centre O. Adjacent pyramids meet in the triangle joining O to their shared cube edge.
